verdict.rationale: Antigravity's own docs describe features that support codebase understanding: subagents for extensive codebase searches, multi-folder Projects that give agents full codebase context, and Artifacts that can include architecture diagrams and implementation plans. None of the evidence describes a dedicated codebase-explanation or entry-point-finding workflow, and no hands-on reports confirm it works for this purpose. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of codebase explanation or architecture mapping, guidance on locating where to start changes, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can understand how a codebase fits together to find where to start making changes

citations.quote: an agent can delegate tasks—such as running tests or performing extensive codebase searches—to dedicated subagents.
a project can work with one folder or multiple folders (e.g., a frontend and a backend repo), providing your agents with all of the context required for your codebase
Artifacts include rich markdown plans (Implementation Plans), code diffs, architecture diagrams, images, and browser recordings.
Planning Mode: The agent plans thoroughly before executing tasks... produces structured implementation plans called Artifacts
